description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting representation scores candidate items by dot product. Attention can emphasize recent interactions or longer-range dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
motivation: Combine the simplicity useful for sparse histories with the ability to capture longer sequential patterns. SASRec is an established starting baseline; the supplied description does not specify a new cold-start mechanism. Learned item embeddings alone cannot reliably represent items without training interactions.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve all four dataset routes. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts within the trial directory. Select using macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and definitions. Architecture changes require matching predictor-writer and diagnostic adaptations. No experiments or performance measurements were performed for this summary.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the prescribed training and validation splits.
  Initialize SASRec with training seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Encode padded histories with causal attention.
    Score next-item positives and sampled negatives.
    Minimize binary cross-entropy over non-padding positions.
  Save model artifacts and compatible predictor code.
Compare trials using host-reported macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Provides a well-defined sequential recommendation baseline.
originality.negative: SASRec is established; no novel cold-start extension is described. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Public titles and descriptions could support a separately evaluated content-aware extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: Any improvement remains hypothetical until validated within the shared search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The prescribed baseline already supplies the central model and dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Changes must keep training, generated prediction code, and diagnostic interfaces consistent.
